events.factual_description: Rhizome DC and Transparent Productions present Sonic Chambers Quartet on Sunday, November 8, 2026. The official presenter page lists doors at 6:30 PM, music at 7:00 PM, and a $20-$30 sliding-scale face price. The lineup is Byron Asher and Tomas Majcherski on reeds, Matt Booth on bass, and Doug Garrison on drums. Rhizome describes the New Orleans/New York project as working between spontaneity and composition. Byron Asher's official project page identifies Asher and Majcherski as clarinetist/saxophonist co-leaders, confirms the same quartet, and states that the collaboration began in 2023. The group's debut album Kiss of the Earth was released in 2025 on 577 Records; the artist/label release page credits Asher on tenor saxophone, clarinet and bass clarinet, Majcherski on tenor and soprano saxophones and clarinet, Booth on bass, and Garrison on drums, and describes the title track as an arrangement of material from Stravinsky's The Rite of Spring reduced to an improvisatory vehicle.

en.why_it_matters: The hook is the sound architecture: two multi-reed players moving among clarinets and saxophones over bass and drums, with composition and spontaneous form treated as parts of the same language. Kiss of the Earth makes that approach concrete—the quartet can move from original material to a Stravinsky-derived framework without turning the music into a repertory exercise. In Rhizome's close room, the interest is hearing color, density and collective decisions change at conversational distance.
en.trip_verdict: If Sunday is open in the DMV, this is a worthwhile Rhizome night for concentrated improvisation and an unusual reed-heavy palette. I would not displace a stronger commitment or build a corridor trip around it.
en.listen_before: Sonic Chambers Quartet — Kiss of the Earth

es.why_it_matters: El gancho está en la arquitectura del sonido: dos multiinstrumentistas de alientos que se mueven entre clarinetes y saxofones sobre bajo y batería, tratando composición y forma espontánea como partes del mismo lenguaje. Kiss of the Earth vuelve concreta esa idea: el cuarteto puede pasar de material original a un marco derivado de Stravinsky sin convertir la música en un ejercicio de repertorio. En la cercanía de Rhizome, interesa escuchar cómo cambian el color, la densidad y las decisiones colectivas casi a distancia de conversación.
es.trip_verdict: Si el domingo está libre en el DMV, vale la pena caer a Rhizome por improvisación concentrada y una paleta cargada hacia los alientos poco común. No desplazaría un compromiso más fuerte ni armaría un viaje por el corredor alrededor de esta fecha.
